rules.text:
**MUST** With organisations enabled, each organisation has one signing secret. Send the human Owner to the dashboard. Never ask for it in chat or expose it to AI tools.\
An authorised server can use an Owner session or the organisation API credential. Admin and Member sessions cannot retrieve it. Store it on the receiving server.
rules.why: All tenant numbers in that organisation share this signing authority.

rules.text: call.bookings has no account field or per-number secret.
rules.instead: After signature verification, look up number in your own tenant table. It is the business to number inbound and from number outbound.

rules.text: Verify X-Nixflex-Signature (t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex>) with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + "." + the original raw request body. Compare the digest in constant time and enforce a freshness policy before trusting the payload.
Set delivery destinations per number. Pre-call settings can be scoped to an agent or number. Keep the delivery destination and your signature-verification secret separate.
These are the top-level call.bookings keys. Use call_id to correlate processing and design for redelivery.
With organisations enabled, only an Owner session or the organisation API credential can retrieve the secret on a server. The kits omit this secret read.
On permission_denied verify the acting role. A client with insufficient authority should never be given the organisation secret.
